Subject: Re: Starter pack — can we stage credits and handle tax treatment?

Hi Mina — great chat earlier. Quick recap and asks from our side so Legal/Finance can sign off:

- LaunchBridge cohort typically receives $10k in free credits from vendors as a ‘starter sweetener’. For this pilot we’d like to split that: $6k as immediate API credits (usable on hosted), and $4k to be held in escrow to convert to a Dedicated discount if the cohort converts within 6 months.
- Our finance team flags that credits delivered as subsidies sometimes trigger taxable income treatment for small non-profits in our cohort. Can you outline how Redwood invoices / documents these credits so we can forward to our tax advisor?
- Can we get a short ALTERNATIVE path: if a startup converts to Dedicated, we’d like the $4k escrow to become a 6-month deferred invoice credit (applied monthly), not a one-time lump credit.

Attached is a draft mutual-action plan and our standard Sponsor addendum (pdf). If you can propose language or a mechanics note we can share with our legal team that would be helpful.

Thanks — Lina
Lina Gomez
Director, Partnerships | LaunchBridge

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear summary and the doc. Happy to propose a mechanics model and the minimal legal/finance language to keep things operationally simple. Two proposed paths below:

Option A — Split + Escrow -> Dedicated conversion (your preferred):
- Issue $6k in standard promo credits on signup (hosted API). Credits appear on the customer billing page as a "Promotional Credit" line item with an issuance date.
- Place $4k into a managed escrow (not yet issued to the customer). If the customer converts to Dedicated within 6 months, the escrowed $4k is released as a deferred invoice credit, applied monthly over the first 6 months of Dedicated billing. If they do not convert within 6 months, the escrow expires and is reclaimed by Redwood operations.
- Tax note: We can issue a Google-style credit memo / grant letter that states the $6k was provided as promotional consideration (non-invoice) and the $4k is contingent upon conversion and will be documented as a post-sale credit (deferred invoice credit) if released. We will provide a PDF credit memo per customer at issuance and a DS-annotation of the invoice sequence when/if the escrow is released.

Option B — Immediate full credits with conversion bonus:
- Issue $10k immediately as credits; on conversion Redwood issues a Dedicated onboarding discount equal to $4k as a separate invoice credit. Easier operationally but less aligned to sponsor visibility.

Operational asks from our side to implement Option A if you prefer it:
1) Signed addendum that defines escrow mechanics (expiry, release triggers).
2) A short tax/legal paragraph we can add to sponsor materials (we’ll draft, you review).
3) Access to a named HubSpot deal id per cohort to automate credit issuance and redemption.

I’ve copied Marissa on the note to coordinate the escrow mechanics and accounting entries. Attached: short sample wording for an addendum.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Growth | Redwood Inference

Forwarding LaunchBridge request — they want Option A (split with $4k escrow to convert into deferred invoice credit applied monthly on Dedicated). Key asks for Finance/Accounting:

- How do we book the $4k escrow on our books? Do we treat as a liability until released? Is there a standard memo we can produce per-customer to minimize taxable ambiguity for the recipient?
- If released as a monthly deferred invoice credit, do we need to create a distinct revenue recognition flow or will a credit memo applied to invoices suffice?
- Any operational limits we want to impose (max per cohort, expiry windows) — LaunchBridge suggests 6 months.

Ben / Marissa — thoughts? If this is acceptable I’ll draft the addendum and push to Lina + legal.

Thanks,
Mina
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Starter pack — can we stage credits and handle tax treatment?

Mina — good proposal. Finance prefers Option A but with a couple constraints to keep GAAP and ops tidy: 

1) Booking: treat escrowed $4k as a contract liability (deferred revenue/contra-revenue) on Redwood's books until release. Provide a per-customer "Grant Letter" that states the credits are promotional and contingent; that should help recipients' tax teams determine local treatment.
2) Release mechanics: when the customer converts, we issue a single credit memo for $4k and then automatically apply it across invoices as a recurring monthly negative invoice line over 6 months (we can implement as 6 equal credit memos or one memo that our billing system allocates).
3) Controls: cap escrow per cohort at $50k total and per-customer at $4k (to limit exposure). Keep the expiry at 6 months but allow an exception route — Sales Ops approval required.

Marissa — please draft the exact addendum clause for escrow and the template Grant Letter. Mina — once Marissa has a draft I’ll sign off and we can share with Lina.

Ben
VP, Growth Partnerships | Redwood Inference
